title: General Chaos
subtitle: A battlefield small enough to command
summary: General Chaos is Game Refuge's comic real-time tactics game, published by Electronic Arts for Genesis in 1993.
body: General Chaos is Game Refuge's comic real-time tactics game, published by Electronic Arts for Genesis in 1993. Rival generals send small teams of specialists into compact battlefields, trying to overcome the opposing force and eventually capture its capital. The soldiers act within the player's orders while the action continues around them. The scale makes individual positions easy to read: a few characters, the weapon each carries and the gap separating them from the enemy form the essential pieces of a battle.

Before fighting, the player chooses a team from several compositions. Most contain five soldiers with different weapons, while a two-person commando team uses a control scheme that grants more direct handling. The selection changes which distances and positions suit the force. Moving one specialist forward can create an opportunity while exposing another part of the team. The animated presentation keeps the war comic, but successful orders still depend on noticing who can attack effectively and who needs to be moved out of trouble.

Brian Colin and Jeff Nauman designed the game, with Colin creating the art and Nauman handling programming. Michael Bartlow composed the music. Battles can be played individually or as a campaign whose strategic map changes with the results. That larger contest gives each quick clash a place in the struggle between Generals Chaos and Havoc. General Chaos turns command into a console-sized activity, combining the immediacy of moving a cursor around a small field with the longer consequences of winning ground across successive encounters.
